 Amid Trade Rumors, Maxx Crosby Playing Better than His Box Scores 
   Raiders Beat Staff  October 24, 2026   2 Comments 
 Maxx Crosby has hit opposing quarterbacks 15 times through six games, yet the trade-deadline talk keeps circling back to the fact that he has only two sacks.
 But of all his stats, the sack total tells you the least about Crosby. 
 Those 15 hits put the Raiders’ edge rusher T-3rd in the NFL, alongside Houston’s Will Anderson Jr. Only Buffalo’s Greg Rousseau (19) and Denver’s Zach Allen (16) have more ( Pro Football Reference ).
 He’s getting home. The quarterback just keeps getting the ball out a half-step early.
 The Chatter
 The Raiders opened 3-0, then dropped three straight: 30-27 to Kansas City, 45-17 at New England and 33-30 to Buffalo. The defense has allowed 30 or more in all three ( Raiders.com ).
 After the New England loss, CBS Sports’ Pete Prisco said Las Vegas should shop him: “Shouldn’t you consider trading [Maxx] Crosby again? Because I would. Because I don’t think he’s part of the future.” He floated Jacksonville as a possible buyer.  As PFN noted , that was his suggestion, not a report of actual talks.
 Earlier, after the Kansas City loss, Jason La Canfora wrote that a rival dangling two first-round picks “might catch Las Vegas’ attention,” and quoted one general manager: “I don’t think the price comes down.” La Canfora’s own read: “Ultimately, I expect him to stay put” ( via Yardbarker ).
 The two-firsts number isn’t random. In March the Raiders agreed to send Crosby to Baltimore for two first-round picks. The Ravens backed out after his medical evaluation following a winter meniscus repair, and the deal was never made official ( PFN ,  Yardbarker ).
 The trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 3 p.m. CT.
 The Hits
 Here’s how Crosby’s 15 hits have stacked up week by week ( Pro Football Reference ): 3 against Miami, 1 against the Chargers, 2 against New Orleans, 5 against Kansas City, 2 at New England and 2 against Buffalo. His sacks: 1.5 in the opener and a half-sack against Kansas City. He hasn’t had one since.
 It isn’t only him. As a team, Las Vegas has 43 QB hits, 6th in the league, but just 15 sacks, 13th ( Pro Football Reference ). The Raiders’ rush is reaching quarterbacks; it just can’t get the follow-through.
 Hits are the better read on a rusher who is winning. Sacks depend on things he doesn’t control: how fast the ball comes out, whether the quarterback steps up, whether the guy across from him gets there first. Hits also put an internal clock in the quarterback’s head, which can throw off timing.
 The Value
 He’s had slow sack starts before: in 2021 he had 5.0 through six weeks and finished with 8.0 ( Pro Football Reference ). The harder question is what that production brings on the trade market, and history says two first over the offseason was incredibly rich.
 Von Miller, 2021.  In his last three full seasons before the trade (2017-19), Miller had 32.5 sacks and 69 QB hits ( Pro Football Reference ). Crosby had 32.0 sacks and 71 QB hits over 2023-25. At the deadline, Denver sent Miller to the Rams for 2022 second- and third-round picks ( TheRams.com ) and paid $9 million of the $9.7 million left on his salary ( LA Times ,  The Athletic ). He was 32 and in the final year of his deal.
 Chandler Jones, 2016.  Jones had 30.0 sacks from 2013-15 and was entering the final year of his rookie deal at $7.79 million ( ESPN ). In March, New England sent him to Arizona for guard Jonathan Cooper and a second-round pick ( Patriots.com ).
 Neither brought two firsts. Rushers who matched Crosby’s sack production went for Day 2 picks. The difference is the contract: both were expiring deals, and Crosby is signed through 2029, which is how the March price reached two firsts. At the deadline, though, the Miller deal is the template: lower picks, with the seller eating salary.
 Teams see the sack total, and it will affect what they’re willing to give up to get him.
 The Streak
 Any team calling about Crosby is buying a rusher who has never finished a season with fewer than 7.0 sacks. Per  Raiders.com , he needs 5.0 more to make it eight straight. That would make him one of nine players since 1982 with 7.0-plus sacks in each of his first eight seasons.
 He has 11 games left to get five.
 The Contract
 The money is part of the trade value, too, and it cuts both ways. Crosby is signed through 2029 on a three-year, $106.5 million extension, an average of $35.5 million, with $91.5 million in practical guarantees,  per Spotrac . His 2026 base salary is $30 million.
 That’s a lot of money for an Edge with only two sacks through six games. In a trade, his salary goes with him unless the Raiders agree to cover part of it, as Denver did with Miller. Only the prorated bonus money already on their books stays behind as dead money: about $5.1 million per  Spotrac . A buyer is paying for the next three years, not the first six weeks of this one. If two firsts was the March number, holding out for a discount because the sack total is light means buying at the wrong time.
 Selling now would mean taking a low offer for a player whose underlying numbers say the sacks are coming.
 The Reality
 If the Raiders do want to shop Crosby again before the deadline, they’d better hope the hits start turning into sacks soon. Right now his sack total undersells what his hits and track record say he is, and offers will reflect that. If trading him is the priority, it’ll probably wait until the offseason. 
 The best option is to keep him a Raider for life.
